source.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Evolutionary Feature Construction in Regression
source.authors: Heng-Zhe Zhang; Qi Chen; Bing Xue; Wolfgang Banzhaf; Meng-Jie Zhang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendices. Some figures and tables are flattened or garbled, but the cited result descriptions and readable tables are intact.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests sharpness-aware generalization in GP-based symbolic regression, a new model and task setting compared with the mapped versions' neural-network classification settings. Its results do not test any version's specified behavior or measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports GP regression results on natural datasets and comparisons involving sharpness, but its subjects and measures do not match the behaviors specified in V1–V8. Cited findings about deep networks are prior work, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses sharpness as an optimization objective for genetic-programming regression and reports its method's performance. It does not test V7's correlation between magnitude-aware weight sharpness and generalization gaps among convolutional networks, or any other supplied version. Its randomly initialized neural-network experiment checks perturbation equivalence, not generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that semantic sharpness-aware optimization improves GP feature-construction generalization relative to cross-validation loss alone and six alternative complexity measures, especially with limited samples or noisy labels, while acknowledging that SAM is not best on every dataset.
record.recipe_differences: The method optimizes cross-validation loss and estimated semantic sharpness in evolutionary GP feature construction for regression, rather than training the neural-network classifiers described by the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports outcome differences across perturbation magnitudes, perturbation iterations, noise types, sharpness aggregation choices, adaptive scaling strategies, and use of the sharpness reduction layer; these analyses concern GP regression.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM-GP significantly improves test R2 over standard GP on 36 of 58 datasets and worsens it on 6, while standard GP has higher training R2 on 54.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining semantic sharpness optimization with cross-validation loss can improve held-out performance in GP feature construction despite lower training performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four representative datasets, training and test R2 are strongly positively correlated during SAM-GP evolution; Figure 8 reports correlations from 0.857 to 0.997.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training and test performance can improve together during sharpness-aware GP evolution.

fits_no_version.finding: With Gaussian noise added to training targets, SAM-GP improves test performance over standard GP on 31 of 36 datasets and over PP on 21, with no reported losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware GP feature construction can improve regression performance with noisy training targets.

record.problems: Experiments use small training samples (typically 100), and the reported comparisons aggregate results across datasets. Some results appear only in figures; no uncertainty intervals are reported for the headline dataset-count comparisons. The study does not test the mapped neural-network claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Figure-only plots and numerous appendix hyperparameter comparisons concern GP regression method choices and do not test any mapped version; they are summarized in method_sensitivity.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance alongside natural-label generalization in the same neural-network recipes.
Test error as network width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning conditions.
Training batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes. Appendix D.2 changes sharpness aggregation, not training batch size.
Dropout effects on classifier test error.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness ranking generalization gaps among convolutional networks with similarly low training loss, including comparisons with norm and margin measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T3 classification with uses_without_test/T4. GP semantic perturbations and comparisons between regularization methods do not establish V7's specified neural-network correlation.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the specified neural-network classifiers.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large-batch training comparisons and recipe changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons among convolutional networks matched on training loss, and the specified norm and margin comparisons.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
